content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The draft specification is ready for review:

- [spec.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- [quality checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)
- Feature directory: `specs/001-bookmark-manager`
- Validation: all 16 quality checks passed; no unresolved clarifications

The proposed first release covers saving, searching, tagging, filtering, favoriting, editing, opening, and deleting personal bookmarks. Accounts, sharing, synchronization, folders, imports, and browser extensions are outside the initial scope.

Please approve the specification or tell me what you’d like changed. I’ll only move to the implementation plan after your approval.

Thanks for putting this together — it's clearly laid out and a lot of it matches what I picture. A few things stand out that I'd want changed before I'm comfortable signing off, and they're all inside the parts you're already covering (saving, searching, tagging).

1. **Saving a link should do more of the work for me.** Right now it says I have to type in the title myself, and it explicitly says the app won't look anything up. That's not what I want. When I paste a web address, I'd expect the app to go grab the page's title (and ideally a short description and the little site icon) and fill those in for me, so I can just tweak them if needed rather than typing everything by hand. Being able to save with almost nothing but the link is a big part of why I'd use this.

2. **Searching needs to be smarter than plain word matching.** A couple of things I'd expect: I want to be able to search my tags directly (something like typing `#recipes` to pull up everything tagged that way), and I want to combine terms — like "this AND that," "one OR the other," "this but NOT that," and putting quotes around a phrase to match it exactly. When my collection gets big, plain partial matching won't be enough to find things.

3. **Tag suggestions while I type.** When I'm adding a tag to a bookmark, I'd want it to suggest tags I've already used so I don't accidentally make three slightly different versions of the same tag.

4. **A "read it later" idea, not just favorites.** Favorites are fine, but the thing I really care about is marking a link as something I still need to read, and then being able to look at just those unread ones on their own. Favoriting my best links and tracking what I haven't gotten to yet feel like two different needs to me.

Everything else — accounts, sharing, syncing, folders, imports, and browser add-ons being left out for now — I'm okay with for a first version. Could you fold these four changes in and show me the updated version?

The updated specification is ready:

- [Updated specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- [Quality checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)

The revision now includes:

- URL-only saving with automatic title, description, and site-icon retrieval
- Graceful fallbacks when page details are unavailable
- Editable retrieved metadata that never overwrites the user’s changes
- `#tag`, `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, quoted-phrase, and parenthesized searches
- Existing-tag suggestions with keyboard support
- Independent favorite and unread/read-later states
- A dedicated unread filter
- Explicit marking as read; merely opening a link does not mark it read

All 16 specification-quality checks pass, with no unresolved clarifications. Please approve this revision or request further changes; once approved, I’ll prepare the implementation plan.

This looks great — you've picked up everything I asked for. Pasting a link and having the title, description, and icon filled in for me (with sensible fallbacks when a page doesn't cooperate), the smarter search with tags, and/or/not, exact phrases and grouping, the tag suggestions so I stop making near-duplicates, and keeping "still need to read" separate from favorites with its own view — that's exactly how I picture using it.

One small thing I noticed and actually like: opening a link doesn't mark it read on its own, only when I say so. That's the behavior I'd want, so please keep it.

I'm happy with this version of the spec. Go ahead and put together the implementation plan — I'll wait to see that before anything gets built.

content:
Bookmark Garden is built and ready to review at:

**http://maker:4000**

Implemented:

- URL-only saving with automatic title, description, and favicon retrieval
- Safe fallbacks that preserve entered content
- Boolean, phrase, grouped, and `#tag` search
- Reusable keyboard-accessible tag suggestions
- Independent favorites and read-later status
- Opening links never marks them read
- Editing and confirmation-protected deletion
- Responsive and accessible interface

Validation is fully green: 73/73 tasks completed, 46 unit/component tests, 29 integration tests, 5 browser journeys, performance testing with 5,000 bookmarks, accessibility checks, OpenAPI linting, and zero reported dependency vulnerabilities.

The review starts with a clean collection. Detailed results are in [validation.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/validation.md).

I took it for a spin and it does everything I asked for. I pasted a link and it pulled in the title, description, and icon on its own; saving with just a URL worked and my own edits stuck. Trying to save the same link again stopped me and pointed me back to the one I already had. Search behaves the way I wanted — I could pull up a tag with `#recipes`, exclude things with NOT, and a broken query gave me a clear "add a tag name" message instead of odd results. Tag suggestions offered up what I'd already used. Favorites and my "still to read" list stayed separate — flipping one didn't disturb the other — and just opening a link left it unread until I said otherwise. Editing and deleting both worked, with delete asking first.

This is what I set out to build, and it holds up. I'm happy to accept it as the first version.

I do have a few things I'd like to explore down the road — being able to tuck links away in an archive rather than only deleting them, and saving a favorite search so I can jump back to it — but those are new ideas for a later round, not anything wrong with what you've delivered. Please just note them for next time.

Nicely done.
